title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
claim: Interfacial coordination and noncovalent ‘ionic glue’ assembly graft rare-earth complexes onto surfaces, MOFs, helices, or nanoparticles and transfer chirality or electronic structure across the interface.
explanation: A La–pcam complex with triflate deposits on Au(111); the asymmetric counterion splits the LUMO while the ligand blocks charge transfer to the substrate. Imine groups anchor Co2+ from a Co-MOF onto a 1D La-MOF, improving dispersion and stability. Linker substitution sets CHOL-TPY conformation so helical nanoribbons accept Eu3+ or Eu(L)3 and transfer chirality, with humidity and temperature responses. Cationic [EuL3]3+ glues anionic Ag nanoparticles into composites encoded by fluorescence intensity, lifetime, and Raman signals.
scope: Surface, MOF-on-MOF, helical-nanoribbon, and nanoparticle assemblies of rare-earth complexes.
conditions: Au(111) electrostatic deposition; imine-mediated MOF-on-MOF grafting; interfacial coordination on helical nanoribbons; opposite-charge nanoparticle assembly.
caveats: Each interface uses a different driving force; the review does not claim one universal grafting protocol.
